 ### WeightSource
 
-**This is the adapter for whatever shape your trainer's weights are in.**
-`WeightSource` defines how you extract your weights for your specific framework.
+`WeightSource` adapts your trainer's weights to the engines. vLLM ships
+[`ModuleSource`](#modulesource) for modules that every rank holds whole; for
+anything else (a pipeline stage, a rank's experts, a Megatron export) you
+typically write your own. Engines receive HF-format names, so any gathering,
+re-fusing or renaming happens in the source.
 
-What an engine gets is always the same: HF-format parameter names, and tensors
-already materialized to their full (unsharded) shape. Whatever gathering,
-re-fusing, dequantizing or renaming that takes belongs inside the source.
+A source implements `metadata` and one or both iteration modes:
 
-A `WeightSource` is **re-iterable** and has two required channels:
+| Method | Yields |
+| ------ | ------ |
+| `metadata` | a `functools.cached_property`: a `ParamMeta` for every parameter of the whole model, identical on every rank; transfers nothing |
+| `iter_full()` | `(name, full tensor)` for each name this rank owns |
+| `iter_local()` | `(name, this rank's piece)` for each name this rank owns |
 
-- **`metadata() -> list[ParamMeta]`** — the name, wire dtype, and full shape of
-  every parameter, *without transferring anything*. Cheap when shapes are known
-  locally (an FSDP `DTensor` knows its global shape); may be expensive on the
-  first call for producers that must materialize to learn shapes (a
-  Megatron-Bridge export), in which case it should cache.
-- **iteration** — yields fully-materialized `(name, tensor)` pairs, one at a
-  time.
+NCCL broadcast, IPC and sharded RDT consume `iter_full()`; NCCL M2N consumes
+`iter_local()`. Each engine checks at `trainer_init` that the source implements
+the mode it needs (`implements_iter_full()` / `implements_iter_local()`).
+
+#### ParamMeta: ownership and layout
 
 ```python
 @dataclass(frozen=True)
 class ParamMeta:
     name: str
     dtype: torch.dtype
-    shape: tuple[int, ...]
+    shape: tuple[int, ...]                           # full HF shape
+    owners: tuple[int, ...] | None = None            # trainer ranks, mesh order; None = all
+    mesh_shape: tuple[int, ...] | None = None        # row-major over owners; default (len(owners),)
+    placements: tuple[Placement, ...] | None = None  # one per mesh axis; None = replicated
 ```
 
-!!! warning "The two channels must agree, element for element"
-    `metadata()` must declare exactly what iteration will yield: the same
-    parameters, in the same order, with the same dtypes and shapes. This is an
-    invariant of the ABC, not of any one backend — a source that reorders, omits,
-    or re-dtypes a parameter between the two channels is broken even if the
-    backend you happen to test against never notices. Backends are free to read
-    both channels and to trust that they match; dense NCCL does, and
-    [enforces it](nccl.md#the-two-weightsource-channels-must-agree).
+- **`owners`** are global trainer ranks, the `rank` on `TrainerInitInfo`.
+- **`placements`** are `Replicate()` or `Shard(dim)`, one per mesh axis, and
+  describe what `iter_local()` yields. `Shard` splits the way `torch.chunk`
+  does. A source without `iter_local()` leaves them unset.
+
+Because metadata is the same on every rank, every engine plans from it without
+exchanging anything. `source.owned_names(rank)` gives the names a rank iterates.
+For example, under pipeline parallelism 2 x tensor parallelism 2 (stage 0 is
+ranks 0–1, stage 1 is ranks 2–3):
+
+| name | owners | placements |
+| ---- | ------ | ---------- |
+| `model.embed_tokens.weight` | `(0, 1)` | `(Shard(0),)` |
+| `model.layers.0.self_attn.o_proj.weight` | `(0, 1)` | `(Shard(1),)` |
+| `model.layers.27.self_attn.o_proj.weight` | `(2, 3)` | `(Shard(1),)` |
+| `lm_head.weight` | `(2, 3)` | `(Shard(0),)` |
 
-Materializing is typically a collective, so **every trainer rank must iterate the
-same source in the same order, in lockstep**, or ranks deadlock. `metadata()` can
-itself be a collective for custom producers, so it too runs on every rank — only
-the sender ships the result.
+#### Iteration
 
-`iter(source)` must yield a *fresh* pass each round.
+Both modes yield exactly `owned_names(rank)`, in metadata order,
+with the declared dtypes and shapes. Either may run collectives among a
+parameter's owners (an FSDP all-gather per tensor or per layer), as long as
+every owner iterates in that order. Each call starts a fresh pass.
+
+Keep names that share a layer index (`model.layers.3.*`) contiguous in
+`metadata`: sharded RDT transfers [a layer at a time](sharded_rdt.md).
 
 #### ModuleSource
 
-`ModuleSource(module)` is the common case, over `module.named_parameters()`. It
-handles plain and FSDP-sharded modules with no special casing: iteration
-all-gathers each `DTensor` via `full_tensor()`, while `metadata()` reads the
-*global* `.shape` / `.dtype` and so never triggers a gather.
+`ModuleSource(model)` covers `module.named_parameters()` when every rank holds
+the whole module. A plain tensor is owned by every rank. A `DTensor` (FSDP2, TP)
+is owned by its device mesh's ranks, with the mesh's shape and placements;
+`iter_full()` yields `full_tensor()` and `iter_local()` yields `to_local()`.
+A `DTensor` with other placements (`Partial`, strided shards) is declared
+replicated, and `iter_local()` gathers it.

-#### `held_names()`: partial ownership
-
-By default every rank is assumed to be able to produce every parameter — which is
-what the source above does, since its bridge gathers across all parallelism before
-yielding. That is simple and always correct, but it means the gather cost is paid
-in full on every rank.
-
-Optionally, you can override `held_names()` when the ranks are split so each holds only part of the
-model. It returns the
-parameter names this rank holds (or `None`, the default, for all of them):
-
-```python
-def held_names(self):
-    # This pipeline stage's layers, and within them only this EP rank's experts.
-    return self._my_stage_names - self._foreign_expert_names
-```
-
-This covers various trainer layouts — pipeline stages (a rank holds some layers),
-expert parallelism (a rank holds some experts), both at once, or a shape that fits
-neither. Backends that can route per parameter (see
-[sharded RDT](sharded_rdt.md)) then pull each name from a rank that actually
-holds it.
-
-Three requirements come with overriding it:
-
-- **`metadata()` must still describe the whole model on every rank.** Only the
-  sender's metadata reaches the inference side, so a rank that reported just its
-  own share would leave the rest silently un-transferred. Sharded RDT cross-checks
-  this across ranks at init.
-- **Every name must be held by at least one rank**, or it can never be served.
-  The engine raises at init naming the first orphan.
-- **Iteration yields `None` for a name this rank does not hold.** The name still
-  appears, in metadata order, so the order check stays aligned across ranks — only
-  the data is absent. Claiming a name and then yielding `None` for it is an error
-  the engine reports by name.
-
-!!! warning "Partial ownership only works with sharded RDT"
-    Only a backend that routes per parameter honours `held_names()`.
-    Broadcast backends ignore it and send every name from every rank, so
-    declaring partial ownership there changes nothing.
-
-#### Gather groups
-
-Some backends transfer a layer at a time rather than a model at a time, so they
-partition `metadata()` into **gather groups**. `layerwise_groups` keys each name
-on the **outermost index segment** it contains, so **a group is one decoder
-layer**, with runs of un-indexed names (the embeddings, the final norm,
-`lm_head`) forming groups of their own where they appear:

-```text

-group 1     model.layers.0.*          <- one decoder layer
-group 2     model.layers.1.*
-...
-group N+1   model.norm.weight, lm_head.weight
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer import ParamMeta, WeightSource
+from vllm.distributed.weight_transfer.base import materialize_full_tensor
+
+
+class PipelineStageSource(WeightSource):
+    """`layout` lists the whole model's (name, dtype, shape, stage) on every
+    rank; `stage_ranks[s]` are stage s's trainer ranks; `module` holds this
+    rank's stage, with HF names."""
+
+    def __init__(self, module, layout, stage_ranks):
+        self._module = module
+        self._layout = layout
+        self._stage_ranks = stage_ranks
+
+    @cached_property
+    def metadata(self):
+        return [
+            ParamMeta(name, dtype, shape, owners=self._stage_ranks[stage])
+            for name, dtype, shape, stage in self._layout
+        ]
+
+    def iter_full(self):
+        params = dict(self._module.named_parameters())
+        for meta in self.metadata:
+            if meta.name in params:
+                yield meta.name, materialize_full_tensor(params[meta.name])

-Keying on the index rather than a literal prefix means no per-architecture table:
-`model.layers.0.`, `model.language_model.layers.0.` (recent Qwen text
-checkpoints), `transformer.h.0.` (GPT-2, Falcon), `backbone.layers.0.` (Mamba)
-and a vision tower's `visual.blocks.0.` all partition the same way. The index
-taken is the *outermost* one, which keeps a MoE layer whole — a per-expert name
-like `model.layers.3.mlp.experts.7.w1` keys on the layer, not the expert.
-
-Group index *g* means the same layer on every rank and every consumer, because
-every side derives it from one rank's `metadata()`. That agreement is what lets a
-backend bound its buffers to one layer and free a layer once everyone is done
-with it.
-
-!!! warning "A leaf module's sources must all fall in one group"
-    The sharded-RDT engine frees a group as soon as its last chunk lands, so a
-    module split across groups would park a pull until the stall watchdog fires.
-    The default partition guarantees this; a `groups()` override must preserve
-    it.
-
-Two hooks follow from this, both with working defaults:
-
-- **`groups()`** — this rank's groups, in metadata order. The default is
-  `layerwise_groups(metadata())` restricted to the groups holding at least one
-  held name. A group with nothing held here is skipped entirely.
-- **`iter_groups()`** — the same stream, batched one group at a time. The default
-  drives `__iter__` and batches its output, checking that names arrive in metadata
-  order. Override it when your framework can produce a whole group in one step:
-  materializing is usually a collective, and driving it per group rather than per
-  tensor turns ~37k generator resumes into ~95 on a per-expert MoE model.
-
-Because `metadata()` order defines the partition, **all names sharing a layer
-index must be contiguous in it**. A source whose natural export order interleaves
-layers — bucketing all the MoE experts together, say — has to reorder before
-returning.

+## Limitations
+
+- **Separate fleets only.** The trainer and the inference workers run on different GPUs; colocated setups need [IPC](ipc.md).
+- **No EPLB.** `enable_eplb=true` is rejected: it rearranges experts at runtime, which invalidates the recorded plan.
+- **Supported loader ops only.** A weight loader that needs real data at init raises (see [the op set](#slices-are-tracked-through-vllms-own-weight-loaders)).
+- Names that share a layer index must be contiguous in `metadata` order.

+@pytest.mark.cpu_test
+@pytest.mark.core_model
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_padding_tokens", [0, 3])
+def test_lfm2_bidirectional_conv_respects_sequence_boundaries(
+    dtype, kernel_size, num_padding_tokens
+):
+    """Packed short sequences must match independent noncausal convolutions."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.models.lfm2 import _bidirectional_conv1d
+
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    lengths = [1, 1, 7, 2]
+    inputs = [torch.randn(n, 8, generator=generator).to(dtype) for n in lengths]
+    weight = torch.randn(8, 1, kernel_size, generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    bias = torch.randn(8, generator=generator).to(dtype)
+    expected = []
+    for x in inputs:
+        y = torch.nn.functional.conv1d(
+            x.T[None].float(),
+            weight.float(),
+            bias.float(),
+            padding=kernel_size // 2,
+            groups=8,
+        )
+        expected.append(y[0, :, : len(x)].T.to(dtype))
+
+    packed = torch.cat(inputs)
+    positions = torch.cat([torch.arange(n) for n in lengths])
+    is_padding = None
+    if num_padding_tokens:
+        # Graph padding may retain positions and values from an earlier batch.
+        packed = torch.cat([packed, torch.full((num_padding_tokens, 8), float("nan"))])
+        positions = torch.cat([positions, torch.arange(2, 2 + num_padding_tokens)])
+        is_padding = torch.arange(len(packed)) >= sum(lengths)
+    actual = _bidirectional_conv1d(
+        packed.to(dtype),
+        weight,
+        bias,
+        positions,
+        is_padding,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual[: sum(lengths)], torch.cat(expected))
+
+

+def _bidirectional_conv1d(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    bias: torch.Tensor | None,
+    positions: torch.Tensor,
+    is_padding: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Same-padding depthwise convolution over packed, complete sequences."""
+    kernel_size = weight.shape[-1]
+    padding = kernel_size // 2
+    # Each encoder request starts at position zero. For packed requests
+    # x = [a0, a1, a2, b0, b1], positions = [0, 1, 2, 0, 1] gives
+    # sequence_ids = [1, 1, 1, 2, 2].
+    sequence_ids = (positions == 0).cumsum(0)
+    if is_padding is not None:
+        # Keep runtime padding (e.g. CUDA graph padding) distinct from real requests.
+        sequence_ids = sequence_ids.masked_fill(is_padding, -2)
+    # With kernel_size=3 and no runtime padding, the example becomes:
+    # padded_ids = [-1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2, -1]
+    # padded_x   = [ 0, a0, a1, a2, b0, b1, 0]
+    padded_ids = F.pad(sequence_ids, (padding, padding), value=-1)
+    padded_x = F.pad(x, (0, 0, padding, padding))
+    output = torch.zeros_like(x, dtype=torch.float32)
+    for tap in range(kernel_size):
+        # Exclude neighbors across request boundaries (e.g. a2 and b0).
+        same_sequence = padded_ids[tap : tap + x.shape[0]] == sequence_ids

+        values = values.masked_fill(~same_sequence[:, None], 0)
+        output = output + values * weight[:, 0, tap].float()

+        output = output + bias.float()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Tests for cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens, the CPU tier capacity at max_model_len."""
+
+import pytest
+
+from tests.v1.kv_offload.conftest import make_offloading_config
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.config import OffloadingGroupConfig
+from vllm.v1.kv_offload.cpu.common import CPUOffloadingInfo
+
+MAX_MODEL_LEN = 36864
+
+# Group shapes as (tokens_per_block, sliding_window_size_in_chunks) pairs.
+FULL_16 = ((16, None),)
+# One full attention group and 6 sliding window groups of 1024 tokens.
+GEMMA = ((16, None),) + ((16, 4),) * 6
+# One full attention group and 9 Mamba groups of one state each.
+GRANITE = ((528, None),) + ((528, 1),) * 9
+# One full attention group and one hidden state group on a smaller block.
+FULL_PLUS_HIDDEN = ((16, None), (8, None))
+# One group of each kind: full attention, a 1024 token window, and Mamba.
+HYBRID = ((16, None), (16, 4), (16, 1))
+
+
+def make_groups(
+    *shapes: tuple[int, int | None],
+) -> tuple[OffloadingGroupConfig, ...]:
+    return tuple(
+        OffloadingGroupConfig(
+            tokens_per_block=tokens_per_block,
+            layer_names=(f"layer.{index}",),
+            group_id=index,
+            sliding_window_size_in_chunks=window_chunks,
+        )
+        for index, (tokens_per_block, window_chunks) in enumerate(shapes)
+    )
+
+
+def size_tokens(
+    shapes: tuple[tuple[int, int | None], ...],
+    blocks_per_chunk: int,
+    num_chunks: int,
+    max_model_len: int = MAX_MODEL_LEN,
+) -> int | None:
+    config = make_offloading_config(
+        groups=make_groups(*shapes),
+        blocks_per_chunk=blocks_per_chunk,
+        max_model_len=max_model_len,
+    )
+    info = CPUOffloadingInfo.from_config(config, num_chunks, kv_bytes_per_chunk=1)
+    return info.cpu_kv_cache_size_tokens
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("shapes", "blocks_per_chunk", "num_chunks", "expected"),
+    [
+        # 4500 * 36864 // 144
+        pytest.param(FULL_16, 16, 4500, 1152000, id="single-full-group"),
+        # 4000 * 36864 // min(144, 16)
+        pytest.param(((16, 16),), 16, 4000, 9216000, id="uniform-swa-4096"),
+        # 4000 * 36864 // min(144, 4)
+        pytest.param(((16, 4),), 16, 4000, 36864000, id="uniform-swa-1024"),
+        # 4000 * 36864 // (144 + 6 * 4)
+        pytest.param(GEMMA, 16, 4000, 877714, id="full-plus-6-swa-1024"),
+        # 8000 * 36864 // (70 + 9 * 1)
+        pytest.param(GRANITE, 1, 8000, 3733063, id="full-plus-9-mamba"),
+        # 8000 * 36864 // min(70, 1)
+        pytest.param(((528, 1),), 1, 8000, 294912000, id="pure-mamba"),
+        # 4500 * 36864 // (144 + 288)
+        pytest.param(FULL_PLUS_HIDDEN, 16, 4500, 384000, id="full-plus-hidden"),
+        # 4000 * 36864 // (144 + 4 + 1)
+        pytest.param(HYBRID, 16, 4000, 989637, id="full-plus-swa-plus-mamba"),
+        # A tier of no slots holds no tokens, which is a known value.
+        pytest.param(FULL_16, 16, 0, 0, id="empty-tier"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_size_tokens_over_model_shapes(
+    shapes: tuple[tuple[int, int | None], ...],
+    blocks_per_chunk: int,
+    num_chunks: int,
+    expected: int,
+) -> None:
+    """A windowed group holds a fixed chunk count, so it raises the capacity."""
+    assert size_tokens(shapes, blocks_per_chunk, num_chunks) == expected
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("shapes", "max_model_len"),
+    [
+        pytest.param(FULL_16, 0, id="max-model-len-not-known"),
+        pytest.param((), MAX_MODEL_LEN, id="no-groups"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_size_tokens_is_none_when_unknown(
+    shapes: tuple[tuple[int, int | None], ...], max_model_len: int
+) -> None:
+    assert size_tokens(shapes, 16, 4500, max_model_len) is None

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+import importlib.util
+import threading
+import time

+
+from tests.v1.kv_connector.umbp_test_utils import (

+    UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler,

+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+
+mori_available = importlib.util.find_spec("mori") is not None
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not (current_platform.is_rocm() and mori_available),
+    reason="UMBP is only available on ROCm with the mori package installed",
+)
+
+
+def test_scheduler_async_lookup_defers_then_returns_hit(monkeypatch):
+    gate = threading.Event()
+    key_calls = 0
+    context_builds = 0
+    original_keys = BlockIdentityCodec.keys_for_topology
+    original_context = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler._build_lookup_context
+
+    def build_context(*args, **kwargs):
+        nonlocal context_builds
+        context_builds += 1
+        return original_context(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    def counted_keys(*args, **kwargs):
+        nonlocal key_calls
+        key_calls += 1
+        return original_keys(*args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(BlockIdentityCodec, "keys_for_topology", counted_keys)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler, "_build_lookup_context", build_context
+    )
+
+    class _GatedHandle(_SchedulerHandle):
+        def lookup(self, keys):
+            gate.wait(timeout=5)
+            return [True] * len(keys)
+
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config(
+            {
+                "mode": "embedded",
+                "lookup_async": True,
+                "load_async": False,
+            }
+        ),
+        _kv_cache_config(),
+        _GatedHandle([]),
+        BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("async")),
+    )
+    request = SimpleNamespace(
+        request_id="async",
+        num_tokens=32,
+        block_hashes=[b"a", b"b"],
+    )
+
+    try:
+        assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (None, False)
+        for _ in range(3):
+            assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (None, False)
+        assert key_calls == 1
+        gate.set()
+        result = (None, False)
+        for _ in range(100):
+            result = scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0)
+            if result != (None, False):
+                break
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+    finally:
+        # Release the gated lookup so close() does not wait for its timeout.
+        gate.set()
+        scheduler.close()
+
+    # The final prompt token must still execute, leaving one reusable block.
+    assert result == (16, False)
+    assert key_calls == 1
+    assert context_builds == 1
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("change", ["local", "length", "hash", "request"])
+def test_async_lookup_discards_results_for_changed_request(monkeypatch, change):
+    """A completed old query must not be interpreted using a new prefix."""
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config({"lookup_async": True}),
+        _kv_cache_config(),
+        _SchedulerHandle([]),
+        BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("changed-query")),
+    )
+    queries = []
+
+    def submit(fn, keys):
+        future: Future[list[bool]] = Future()
+        queries.append((keys, future))
+        return future
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(scheduler._lookup_executor, "submit", submit)
+    request = SimpleNamespace(
+        request_id="r", num_tokens=49, block_hashes=[b"a", b"b", b"c"]
+    )
+    try:
+        assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (None, False)
+        queries[0][1].set_result([True] * len(queries[0][0]))
+        local_tokens = 0
+        if change == "local":
+            local_tokens = 16
+        elif change == "length":
+            request.num_tokens = 65
+            request.block_hashes.append(b"d")
+        elif change == "hash":
+            request.block_hashes[-1] = b"different"
+        else:
+            request = SimpleNamespace(**vars(request))
+        assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, local_tokens) == (
+            None,
+            False,
+        )
+        assert len(queries) == 2
+        queries[1][1].set_result([False] * len(queries[1][0]))
+        assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, local_tokens) == (0, False)
+    finally:
+        scheduler.close()
+
+
+def test_scheduler_reset_clears_pending_lookup_state(monkeypatch):
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config({"mode": "embedded", "lookup_async": True}),
+        _kv_cache_config(),
+        _SchedulerHandle([]),
+        BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("reset")),
+    )
+    try:
+        future: Future[list[bool]] = Future()
+        monkeypatch.setattr(scheduler._lookup_executor, "submit", lambda *a: future)
+        request = SimpleNamespace(request_id="req", num_tokens=32, block_hashes=[b"a"])
+        assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (None, False)
+        scheduler._load_specs["req"] = LoadSpec(0, 16)
+
+        assert scheduler.reset_store()
+        assert future.cancelled()
+        assert scheduler._pending_lookups == {}
+        assert scheduler._load_specs == {}
+    finally:
+        scheduler.close()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure", [TimeoutError("lookup timeout"), [True, False]])
+def test_async_lookup_failure_recomputes_and_allows_retry(failure):
+    class _Handle(_SchedulerHandle):

+def test_external_chunked_local_hit_preserves_absolute_positions(
+    chunk_object_resident, lookup_async
+):
+    """A chunked-local hit is claimed only through resident absolute chunks.
+
+    With a 16-token local prefix, claiming token 80 needs the group-1 object
+    for tokens 64-79. When it is missing, the safe boundary is the token-64
+    chunk start, so 48 external tokens are claimed and nothing loads it.
+    """
+    config = _kv_cache_config()
+    full = config.kv_cache_groups[0].kv_cache_spec
+    config.kv_cache_groups.append(
+        KVCacheGroupSpec(
+            ["chunked"],
+            ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec(
+                block_size=16,
+                num_kv_heads=full.num_kv_heads,
+                head_size=full.head_size,
+                dtype=full.dtype,
+                attention_chunk_size=64,
+            ),
+        )
+    )
+    codec = BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("absolute-chunk"))
+    hashes = [b"a", b"b", b"c", b"d", b"e"]
+    hits = {
+        codec.key(block_hash, group_id): True
+        for group_id in (0, 1)
+        for block_hash in hashes[1:]
+    }
+    if not chunk_object_resident:
+        del hits[codec.key(b"e", 1)]
+    handle = _SchedulerHandle(hits)
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config({"lookup_async": lookup_async}), config, handle, codec
+    )
+    pool = BlockPool(8, True, 16)
+    for group_id in (0, 1):
+        identity = make_block_hash_with_group_id(hashes[0], group_id)
+        pool.cached_block_hash_to_block.insert(identity, pool.blocks[group_id + 1])
+    scheduler.bind_gpu_block_pool(pool)
+    request = make_request(
+        "chunked",
+        num_tokens=81,
+        block_hashes=hashes,
+        block_ids=([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [0, 0, 0, 0, 6]),
+    )
+    external_tokens = 64 if chunk_object_resident else 48
+    try:
+        result = scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 16)
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 5
+        while result[0] is None and time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            time.sleep(0.001)
+            result = scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 16)
+        assert result == (external_tokens, True)
+        scheduler.update_state_after_alloc(
+            request,
+            SimpleNamespace(get_block_ids=lambda group_ids: request.block_ids),
+            external_tokens,
+        )
+        plans = scheduler._pending_loads[request.request_id]
+        expected = [(0, 2), (0, 3), (0, 4)]
+        if chunk_object_resident:
+            expected += [(0, 5), (1, 6)]
+        assert [(plan.group_id, plan.block_id) for plan in plans] == expected
+        loaded_keys = [plan.key for plan in plans]
+        assert (codec.key(b"e", 1) in loaded_keys) == chunk_object_resident
+    finally:
+        scheduler.close()
+

+def test_hybrid_shadow_lookup_cleans_up_after_failure(monkeypatch, failure_stage):
+    """A failed query cannot leak shadow hits or consume pool capacity."""
+    handle = _SchedulerHandle({})
+    codec = BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("shadow-cleanup"))
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config({}), _hybrid_kv_cache_config(), handle, codec
+    )
+    request = make_request("r", num_tokens=33)
+    handle.hits = {codec.key(h, g): True for h in request.block_hashes for g in (0, 1)}
+    coordinator = scheduler._lookup_coordinator
+    pool = coordinator.block_pool
+    free_blocks = pool.get_num_free_blocks()
+
+    def fail(*args, **kwargs):
+        raise RuntimeError("injected shadow failure")
+
+    try:
+        with monkeypatch.context() as patch:
+            if failure_stage == "lookup":
+                lookup = pool.get_cached_block
+
+                def fail_after_lookup(*args, **kwargs):
+                    lookup(*args, **kwargs)
+                    fail()
+
+                patch.setattr(pool, "get_cached_block", fail_after_lookup)
+            else:
+                patch.setattr(coordinator, "find_longest_cache_hit", fail)
+            with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="injected shadow failure"):
+                scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0)
+        assert pool.get_num_free_blocks() == free_blocks
+        assert len(pool.cached_block_hash_to_block) == 0
+        assert not pool.cached_block_hashes_by_block
+        assert pool.hits == []
+        assert pool.hit_blocks == {}
+        handle.hits = {}
+        assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (0, False)
+        handle.hits = {
+            codec.key(h, g): True for h in request.block_hashes for g in (0, 1)
+        }
+        assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (32, True)
+        assert pool.get_num_free_blocks() == free_blocks

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("boundary", [0, 3, 8, 11, 12, 16])
+def test_scheduler_accepts_only_computed_hash_aligned_tail(boundary, monkeypatch):
+    # Core hashes requests in 4-token units.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        umbp_scheduler, "resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes", lambda *args: (16, 4)
+    )
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config({"mode": "embedded", "load_async": False}),
+        _kv_cache_config(),
+        _SchedulerHandle([]),
+        BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("partial")),
+    )
+    request = make_request(
+        "partial",
+        num_tokens=12,
+        block_hashes=[b"a", b"b", b"c"],
+        block_ids=([7],),
+        num_computed_tokens=12,
+    )
+    scheduler.update_state_after_alloc(
+        request,
+        SimpleNamespace(get_block_ids=lambda group_ids: ([7],)),
+        0,
+    )
+
+    pool = BlockPool(8, True, 4)
+    scheduler.bind_gpu_block_pool(pool)
+    assert not scheduler.register_finished_partial_tail(
+        request, ([7],), [(0, 7, boundary)]
+    )
+    metadata = scheduler.build_connector_meta(make_scheduler_output())
+
+    assert len(metadata.store_plans) == (1 if boundary == 12 else 0)
+    if metadata.store_plans:
+        tail = metadata.store_plans[0]
+        assert tail.block_id == 7
+        assert tail.key == scheduler.codec.key(b"c", tail.group_id)
+
+
+def test_scheduler_stores_exact_hybrid_boundary_state():
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config({"mode": "embedded", "load_async": False}),

+    request = make_request(
+        "hybrid",

+        num_computed_tokens=16,
+    )
+    scheduler.update_state_after_alloc(
+        request,
+        SimpleNamespace(get_block_ids=lambda group_ids: ([1, 2], [8, 9])),
+        0,
+    )
+    metadata = scheduler.build_connector_meta(
+        make_scheduler_output(
+            block_state=SimpleNamespace(

+    assert plan.key == scheduler.codec.key(b"a", 1)

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("local_tokens", [0, 16])
+def test_scheduler_partial_prefix_loads_full_page_at_absolute_index(
+    local_tokens, monkeypatch
+):
+    # Core hashes requests in 4-token units.
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        umbp_scheduler, "resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes", lambda *args: (16, 4)
+    )
+    config = _kv_cache_config()
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config(
+            {
+                "mode": "embedded",
+                "load_async": False,
+                "enable_partial_hash_hits": True,
+            }
+        ),
+        config,
+        _SchedulerHandle(
+            [False, False, True] + [False] * (4 if local_tokens == 0 else 0)
+        ),
+        BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("partial-prefix")),
+    )
+    request = make_request(
+        "partial-prefix",
+        num_tokens=32,
+        block_hashes=[b"a", b"b", b"c", b"d", b"e", b"f", b"g", b"h"],
+    )
+
+    assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, local_tokens) == (12, False)
+    scheduler.update_state_after_alloc(
+        request,
+        SimpleNamespace(
+            get_block_ids=lambda group_ids: ([6, 7] if local_tokens else [7],)
+        ),
+        12,
+    )
+    plans = scheduler._pending_loads["partial-prefix"]

+    assert len(plans) == 1
+    assert plans[0].block_id == 7

+def test_hybrid_fine_hash_lookup_is_not_limited_by_gpu_page_count():
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config(
+            {"load_async": False, "enable_partial_hash_hits": True},
+            prefix_match_unit=4,
+        ),
+        _hybrid_kv_cache_config(),
+        _SchedulerHandle([True] * 62),
+        BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("many-hashes")),
+    )
+    try:
+        request = make_request(
+            "many-hashes",
+            num_tokens=128,
+            block_hashes=[bytes([index]) for index in range(32)],
+        )
+        for _ in range(2):
+            # Mamba-style groups always load asynchronously.
+            assert scheduler.get_num_new_matched_tokens(request, 0) == (124, True)
+    finally:

+def test_finished_hybrid_tail_pins_full_pages_until_all_workers_finish():
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config(
+            {"mode": "embedded", "load_async": False},
+            prefix_match_unit=4,
+            world_size=2,
+        ),
+        _hybrid_kv_cache_config(),
+        _SchedulerHandle([]),
+        BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("multi-partial")),
+    )
+    request = make_request(
+        "multi-partial",
+        block_hashes=[b"a", b"b", b"c"],
+        block_ids=([7], [9]),
+        num_computed_tokens=12,
+    )
+    scheduler.update_state_after_alloc(
+        request,
+        SimpleNamespace(get_block_ids=lambda group_ids: ([7], [9])),
+        0,
+    )
+
+    pool = BlockPool(16, True, 4)
+    scheduler.bind_gpu_block_pool(pool)
+    blocks = [pool.blocks[7], pool.blocks[9]]
+    pool.touch(blocks)
+    assert not scheduler.register_finished_partial_tail(
+        request,
+        ([7], [9]),
+        [(1, 9, 12)],
+    )
+    assert [block.ref_cnt for block in blocks] == [2, 2]
+    assert scheduler.request_finished(request, ([7], [9])) == (False, None)
+    pool.free_blocks(blocks)
+    assert [block.ref_cnt for block in blocks] == [1, 1]
+    assert scheduler.has_pending_push_work()
+    metadata = scheduler.build_connector_meta(
+        make_scheduler_output(finished={request.request_id})
+    )
+
+    assert len(metadata.store_plans) == 2
+    assert {(plan.group_id, plan.block_id) for plan in metadata.store_plans} == {
+        (0, 7),
+        (1, 9),
+    }
+    assert [block.ref_cnt for block in blocks] == [1, 1]
+    for rank in range(2):
+        scheduler.update_connector_output(
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                kv_connector_worker_meta=UMBPConnectorWorkerMetadata(
+                    store_events={metadata.store_event: StoreEventResult(1)}
+                )
+            )
+        )
+        assert [block.ref_cnt for block in blocks] == ([1, 1] if rank == 0 else [0, 0])
+    assert not scheduler.has_pending_push_work()

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("failure", [None, "missing-rank", "exception", "short"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("restored_tokens", [32, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("null_block", [False, True])
+def test_eager_restored_prefix_rechecks_residency_per_group_and_rank(
+    failure, restored_tokens, null_block, monkeypatch
+):
+    """Only currently complete objects may skip store; fresh suffixes still store."""
+    config = _kv_cache_config()
+    config.kv_cache_groups.append(
+        KVCacheGroupSpec(
+            ["other"], replace(config.kv_cache_groups[0].kv_cache_spec, block_size=32)
+        )
+    )
+    codec = BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("eager-residency"))
+    topology = RankTopology(tp_size=2)
+    handle = _SchedulerHandle({})
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config({"mode": "embedded"}, tensor_parallel_size=2, world_size=2),
+        config,
+        handle,
+        codec,
+        topology,
+    )
+    request = make_request(
+        "req",
+        num_tokens=65,
+        block_hashes=[b"a", b"b", b"c", b"d"],
+        block_ids=([1, 2, 3, 4], [NULL_BLOCK_ID if null_block else 5, 6]),
+        num_computed_tokens=63,
+    )
+    scheduler.update_state_after_alloc(
+        request, SimpleNamespace(get_block_ids=lambda group_ids: request.block_ids), 0
+    )
+    tracker = scheduler._request_trackers["req"]
+    # The group hit windows can be sparse; a scalar watermark cannot deduplicate.
+    tracker.load_spec = LoadSpec(0, restored_tokens, ((None, b"b"), (b"b",)))
+    keys = [
+        key
+        for group, block_size in scheduler.group_block_sizes.items()
+        for end in range(block_size, restored_tokens + 1, block_size)
+        if request.block_ids[group][end // block_size - 1] != NULL_BLOCK_ID
+        for block_hash in (request.block_hashes[end // 16 - 1],)
+        for key in codec.keys_for_topology(block_hash, topology, (group,))
+    ]
+    handle.hits = dict.fromkeys(keys, True)
+    if failure == "missing-rank":
+        handle.hits[keys[1]] = False
+    elif failure == "short":
+        handle.hits = [True]
+    elif failure == "exception":
+
+        def unavailable(keys):
+            raise TimeoutError("lookup unavailable")
+
+        monkeypatch.setattr(handle, "lookup", unavailable)
+    output = make_scheduler_output(new_reqs=[request], scheduled_tokens={"req": 1})
+    created = []
+
+    def record_plan(**kwargs):
+        plan = BlockTransferPlan(**kwargs)
+        created.append(plan)
+        return plan
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        "vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.umbp.scheduler.BlockTransferPlan",
+        record_plan,
+    )
+    try:
+        meta = scheduler.build_connector_meta(output)
+        expected = {(0, b"c"), (0, b"d"), (1, b"d")} if restored_tokens == 32 else set()
+        if failure == "missing-rank":
+            expected.add((0, b"a"))
+        elif failure is not None:
+            expected = {(0, h) for h in request.block_hashes} | {(1, b"b"), (1, b"d")}
+        if null_block:
+            expected.discard((1, b"b"))
+        assert {p.key for p in meta.iter_store_plans()} == {
+            scheduler.codec.key(h, g) for g, h in expected
+        }
+        assert len(meta.store_requests.get("req", [])) == len(expected)
+        # The scheduler keeps eager stores columnar; plans are materialized
+        # only by compatibility iteration or a runtime fallback.
+        assert created == []
+    finally:
+        scheduler.close()
+
+
+def test_several_cache_groups_load_asynchronously():
+    config = _kv_cache_config()
+    config.kv_cache_groups.append(
+        KVCacheGroupSpec(["other"], config.kv_cache_groups[0].kv_cache_spec)
+    )
+    scheduler = UMBPStoreConnectorScheduler(
+        _vllm_config({"mode": "embedded", "load_async": False}),
+        config,
+        _SchedulerHandle([]),
+        BlockIdentityCodec(UMBPNamespace("groups-async")),
+    )
+
+    assert scheduler.load_async
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("several_groups", [False, True])
+def test_several_cache_groups_report_failed_loads_per_request(several_groups):
+    """Core maps block-level load failures to requests only with one group."""
+
+    class _FailingLoadHandle(_WorkerHandle):
+        def load(self, plans):
+            job = TransferJobState(tuple(plans))
+            job.start()
+            job.fail([plan.key for plan in plans], "evicted")
+            return job
+
+    worker = UMBPStoreConnectorWorker(
+        _FailingLoadHandle(), report_failed_requests=several_groups
+    )
+    plan = BlockTransferPlan("key", 3, request_id="req", group_id=0)
+    worker.start_load_kv(
+        None, UMBPConnectorMetadata(async_load=True, load_requests={"req": [plan]})
+    )
+
+    assert worker.get_finished(set()) == (None, {"req"})
+    assert worker.get_failed_recving() == ({"req"} if several_groups else set())
+    assert worker.get_block_ids_with_load_errors() == (set() if several_groups else {3})

+    "vllm/vllm-openai:latest-aarch64${suffix}"

+publish_optional_family() {

+  local staging="public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-release-repo"

+# AWS EFA variant of a vllm-openai image. Adds the EFA userspace stack
+# (libfabric, aws-ofi-nccl, hwloc), the EFA Mooncake wheel (x86_64 only),
+# and DeepEP rebuilt from the amazon-contributing fork for NCCL GIN over EFA.
+#
+# The base must be built with INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true (NIXL and Mooncake):
+#   docker build -f docker/Dockerfile.efa \
+#       --build-arg BASE_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai:latest -t vllm:openai-efa docker/
+#
+# The host still provides the EFA kernel module and memlock limits.
+ARG BASE_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai:latest
+FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}
+
+ARG TARGETARCH
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION=1.51.0
+ARG EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256=83993044fa4df3dc2f8b5c2f7051d61b9689441be023a2c92ea51d3f53f2465c
+
+# Without the KV connectors there is no NIXL plugin or Mooncake wheel to use EFA.
+RUN set -eu; \
+    if ! python3 -c "import importlib.metadata as m; m.version('nixl')" \
+            2>/dev/null; then \
+        echo "Dockerfile.efa needs a base image built with \
+--build-arg INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true" >&2; \
+        exit 1; \
+    fi
+
+# Install the AWS EFA userspace stack.
+RUN set -eux; \
+    EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE="/tmp/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz"; \
+    curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors \
+        "https://efa-installer.amazonaws.com/aws-efa-installer-${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}.tar.gz" \
+        -o "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}"; \
+    echo "${EFA_INSTALLER_SHA256}  ${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" | sha256sum -c -; \
+    tar -xzf "${EFA_INSTALLER_ARCHIVE}" -C /tmp; \
+    # The installer apt-installs dependencies; the base image purged the lists.
+    apt-get update -y; \
+    # Minimal install: libfabric, aws-ofi-nccl and hwloc only. --build-ngc
+    # implies --skip-kmod --skip-limit-conf --no-verify.
+    (cd /tmp/aws-efa-installer && \
+        ./efa_installer.sh --skip-mpi --skip-rdma-core --build-ngc); \
+    test -x /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info; \
+    /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info --version; \
+    # `-l` lists providers without EFA hardware, so this works in a build.
+    /opt/amazon/efa/bin/fi_info -l | grep -q '^efa:'; \

+        -print -quit); \
+    test -n "${EFA_NIXL_PLUGIN}"; \
+    ldd "${EFA_NIXL_PLUGIN}" | grep -q 'libfabric\.so\.1 => /opt/amazon/efa/lib/'; \
+    # Plugins that NCCL_NET_PLUGIN=ofi and NCCL_TUNER_PLUGIN=ofi resolve to.

+    set -eu; \
+    pkg_version() { python3 -c "import importlib.metadata as m, sys; \
+print(m.version(sys.argv[1]))" "$1" 2>/dev/null; }; \
+    if MOONCAKE_VERSION=$(pkg_version mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13); then \
+        MOONCAKE_PKG=mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13; \
+        MOONCAKE_EFA_PKG=mooncake-transfer-engine-efa-cuda13; \
+    elif MOONCAKE_VERSION=$(pkg_version mooncake-transfer-engine); then \
+        MOONCAKE_PKG=mooncake-transfer-engine; \
+        MOONCAKE_EFA_PKG=mooncake-transfer-engine-efa; \
+    else \
+        echo "No Mooncake wheel in the base image; build it with \
+--build-arg INSTALL_KV_CONNECTORS=true" >&2; \
+        exit 1; \
+    fi; \
+    if [ "${TARGETARCH}" != "amd64" ]; then \
+        echo "TARGETARCH=${TARGETARCH}: ${MOONCAKE_EFA_PKG} is x86_64-only, \
+keeping ${MOONCAKE_PKG} (Mooncake EFA protocol unavailable)"; \
+    else \

+${MOONCAKE_EFA_PKG}==${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \

+        uv pip install --system --no-deps \
+            "${MOONCAKE_EFA_PKG}==${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \
+        test "$(pkg_version "${MOONCAKE_EFA_PKG}")" = "${MOONCAKE_VERSION}"; \
+        # `! cmd` is exempt from `set -e`, so check explicitly.
+        if pkg_version "${MOONCAKE_PKG}" >/dev/null; then \
+            echo "${MOONCAKE_PKG} is still installed" >&2; \
+            exit 1; \
+        fi; \
+    fi

+# whose deepep_v2 backend carries EP traffic over EFA through NCCL GIN.
+ARG DEEPEP_REPO="https://github.com/amazon-contributing/DeepEP.git"
+ARG DEEPEP_REF="874779c9ccd2294b56304bd6cc5f138f1f71d097"
+ARG DEEPEP_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="9.0a;10.0a;10.3a"

+# that are absent.

+    CUDA_PKG_VERSION=$(nvcc --version \
+        | grep -oP 'release \K[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | tr '.' '-'); \
+    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update -y; \
+    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get reinstall -y --no-install-recommends \
+        git \
+        libcusparse-dev-${CUDA_PKG_VERSION} \
+        libcusolver-dev-${CUDA_PKG_VERSION} \
+        cuda-nvrtc-dev-${CUDA_PKG_VERSION}; \
+    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
+
+RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/opt/uv/cache \
+    set -eux; \
+    git clone "${DEEPEP_REPO}" /tmp/deepep; \
+    cd /tmp/deepep; \
+    git checkout "${DEEPEP_REF}"; \
+    git submodule update --init --recursive; \
+    uv pip uninstall --system deep_ep 2>/dev/null || true; \
+    NCCL_ROOT="$(python3 -c "import importlib.util, os; \
+s = importlib.util.find_spec('nvidia.nccl'); \
+print(os.path.dirname(s.origin or s.submodule_search_locations[0]))")/nccl"; \
+    export EP_NCCL_ROOT_DIR="${NCCL_ROOT}"; \
+    export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${NCCL_ROOT}/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"; \
+    # The CUDA driver stubs let DeepEP link libcuda in a builder with no driver.
+    export LIBRARY_PATH="${NCCL_ROOT}/lib:/usr/local/cuda/lib64/stubs:\
+/usr/local/cuda/targets/x86_64-linux/lib/stubs:${LIBRARY_PATH:-}"; \
+    export DISABLE_AGGRESSIVE_PTX_INSTRS=1; \
+    export TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST="${DEEPEP_CUDA_ARCH_LIST}"; \
+    uv pip install --system --no-deps -vv --no-build-isolation .; \
+    cd /; \
+    rm -rf /tmp/deepep; \
+    # vLLM only logs when the deepep_v2 backend is unavailable, so fail here.
+    python3 -c "import deep_ep; assert hasattr(deep_ep, 'ElasticBuffer'), \
+'DeepEP built without the ElasticBuffer (v2) API'"
+
+# Provenance. Build args from docker-build-metadata-args.sh override the values
+# inherited from the base image; without them the base's values are kept.
+ARG BASE_IMAGE
+ARG VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT
+ARG VLLM_BUILD_PIPELINE
+ARG VLLM_BUILD_URL
+ARG VLLM_IMAGE_TAG
+ENV VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT=${VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT} \
+    VLLM_BUILD_PIPELINE=${VLLM_BUILD_PIPELINE} \
+    VLLM_BUILD_URL=${VLLM_BUILD_URL} \
+    VLLM_IMAGE_TAG=${VLLM_IMAGE_TAG}
+LABEL org.opencontainers.image.revision="${VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT}" \
+      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VLLM_IMAGE_TAG}" \
+      org.opencontainers.image.url="${VLLM_BUILD_URL}" \
+      ai.vllm.build.commit="${VLLM_BUILD_COMMIT}" \
+      ai.vllm.build.pipeline="${VLLM_BUILD_PIPELINE}" \
+      ai.vllm.build.url="${VLLM_BUILD_URL}" \
+      ai.vllm.image.tag="${VLLM_IMAGE_TAG}" \
+      ai.vllm.efa.base-image="${BASE_IMAGE}" \
+      ai.vllm.efa.installer-version="${EFA_INSTALLER_VERSION}"

 | `secondary_tiers` | no | `[]` | multi-tier | List of secondary tier configs (see below). |
 | `tier_poll_interval_s` | no | `0.001` | multi-tier | Pause between tier-poll rounds for tiers that must be serviced between engine steps (currently `p2p`). See [Threading model](#threading-model). Set to `0` to disable the thread and service those tiers once per engine step instead. |
 | `offload_prompt_only` | no | `true` | both | If `true`, only prompt (prefill) blocks are offloaded; decode blocks are skipped. |
+| `sync_load_budget_bytes` | no | `0` | both | Per-step budget of KV bytes (per GPU) loaded within the same step, so those requests run immediately instead of waiting a step for an async load. Hits that don't fit the remaining budget, or would leave nothing to compute, stay async. `0` disables. |
 | `self_describing_kv_events` | no | `false` | both | Opt-in. When `true` *and* KV cache events are enabled (`--kv-events-config` with `enable_kv_cache_events`), the connector emits self-describing block-granular `BlockStored`/`BlockRemoved` payloads (constituent block hashes, whole-chunk `token_ids`, per-block `block_size`, parent hash, LoRA + group/cache-spec metadata) instead of the placeholder fallback, so external KV-event consumers can index offloaded blocks. Inert unless events are enabled. With `TieringOffloadingSpec`, a CPU promotion is self-describing when a local request observes its primary-tier `HIT` before event translation; otherwise its stored event may retain the placeholder, while a later `HIT` can backfill metadata for removal. Pending-removal/re-promotion races and externally initiated promotions may also produce placeholders, and consumers must ignore removals for unknown hashes. Partial recurrent tails emit the hash-aligned portion from the physical block start through the tail boundary. Other sliding-window/SSM chunks keep the placeholder fallback. In chunk mode (`block_size` > GPU block size, or `blocks_per_chunk` > 1), overlapping chunks re-announce shared per-block hashes, so consumers must reference-count (deduplicate) repeated store/remove announcements. |
 | `spec_module_path` | no | — | both | Python import path for a custom `OffloadingSpec` not in the built-in registry. Required only when `spec_name` is not built-in (advanced). |
 | `canonical_layout` | no | `false` | both | Store each offloaded block in a common canonical representation instead of each worker's local GPU page (enables sharing across TP sizes and single-copy storage of replicated KV). See [Canonical Layout](#canonical-layout). |

+def test_full_replay_with_slow_subscriber(publisher_config, subscriber):
+    """Repeated replays exceeding the default HWM must include every batch and
+    marker, even after earlier replays leave ZMQ's read acknowledgements stale."""
+    steps = publisher_config.buffer_steps = 2500
+    publisher_config.hwm = steps + 1
+    pub = EventPublisherFactory.create(publisher_config, DP_RANK)
+    replay = subscriber.replay_sockets[0]
+    batch = create_test_events(1)
+    try:
+        for _ in range(steps):
+            pub.publish(batch)
+        for _ in range(steps):
+            assert subscriber.receive_one(timeout=1000) is not None
+
+        for first_seq in range(4):
+            subscriber.request_replay(0)
+            assert replay.poll(1000), "Replay did not start"
+            # Leave replay unread until the publisher sends another live batch:
+            # the same thread must finish the entire replay burst before doing so.
+            pub.publish(batch)
+            assert subscriber.receive_one(timeout=1000) is not None
+
+            for expected_seq in range(first_seq, first_seq + steps):
+                assert replay.poll(1000), (
+                    f"Replay {first_seq} stalled before seq {expected_seq}"
+                )
+                delimiter, topic, seq, payload = replay.recv_multipart()
+                assert delimiter == b"" and topic == subscriber.topic_bytes
+                assert int.from_bytes(seq, "big") == expected_seq
+                assert payload
+            assert replay.poll(1000), f"Replay {first_seq} missing end marker"
+            assert replay.recv_multipart() == [
+                b"",
+                b"",
+                ZmqEventPublisher.END_SEQ,
+                b"",
+            ]
+    finally:
+        pub.shutdown()

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("async_scheduling", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("lookahead", [0, 1])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ending", ["prefill", "accepted", "stop", "rejected"])
+def test_finished_spec_request_caches_completed_blocks(
+    async_scheduling, lookahead, ending
+):
+    """Final output can make a computed block's hash available before freeing it."""
+    block_size = 4
+    init_none_hash(sha256)
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        enable_prefix_caching=True,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        num_speculative_tokens=2,
+        speculative_method="ngram_gpu",
+        async_scheduling=async_scheduling,
+    )
+    hasher = get_request_block_hasher(block_size, sha256, lookahead)
+    prompt = list(range(4 if ending == "prefill" else 2))
+    request = Request(
+        request_id="producer",
+        prompt_token_ids=prompt,
+        sampling_params=SamplingParams(
+            max_tokens={"prefill": 1, "rejected": 2}.get(ending, 4),
+            ignore_eos=True,
+            stop_token_ids=[4] if ending == "stop" else None,
+        ),
+        pooling_params=None,
+        block_hasher=hasher,
+    )
+
+    def finish_step(output, tokens):
+        scheduler.update_from_output(
+            output,
+            ModelRunnerOutput(
+                req_ids=[request.request_id],
+                req_id_to_index={request.request_id: 0},
+                sampled_token_ids=[tokens],
+            ),
+        )
+
+    scheduler.add_request(request)
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    if ending == "prefill":
+        finish_step(output, [4])
+    else:
+        finish_step(output, [2])
+        scheduler.update_draft_token_ids(
+            DraftTokenIds(req_ids=[request.request_id], draft_token_ids=[[3, 4]])
+        )
+        output = scheduler.schedule()
+        finish_step(output, [8] if ending == "rejected" else [3, 4, 5])
+
+    assert request.is_finished()
+    assert request.num_output_placeholders == 0
+    probe = Request(
+        request_id="probe",
+        prompt_token_ids=list(request.all_token_ids) + [99] * block_size,
+        sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=1),
+        pooling_params=None,
+        block_hasher=hasher,
+    )
+    expected = 0 if ending == "rejected" else block_size
+    assert scheduler.kv_cache_manager.get_computed_blocks(probe)[1] == expected
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("recovery", ["resident", "preempt", "reset"])
+def test_streaming_lookahead_hashes_follow_recomputed_kv(recovery):
+    """Recomputation uses the continuation's tokens without re-keying resident KV."""
+    block_size = 4
+    model_config = ModelConfig(
+        model="Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct",
+        max_model_len=128,
+        skip_tokenizer_init=True,
+    )
+    scheduler = create_scheduler(
+        model=model_config.model,
+        max_model_len=128,
+        max_num_batched_tokens=128,
+        enable_prefix_caching=True,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        speculative_config=SpeculativeConfig(
+            method="mtp",
+            num_speculative_tokens=1,
+            target_model_config=model_config,
+            target_parallel_config=ParallelConfig(),
+        ),
+    )
+    assert scheduler.num_hash_lookahead_tokens == 1
+    init_none_hash(sha256)
+    hasher = get_request_block_hasher(block_size, sha256, 1)
+
+    def request(request_id, tokens, max_tokens=16, resumable=False):
+        return Request(
+            request_id=request_id,
+            prompt_token_ids=list(tokens),
+            sampling_params=SamplingParams(max_tokens=max_tokens, ignore_eos=True),
+            pooling_params=None,
+            block_hasher=hasher,
+            resumable=resumable,
+        )
+
+    session = request("session", [1, 2, 3], max_tokens=2, resumable=True)
+    scheduler.add_request(session)
+
+    def step(token):
+        output = scheduler.schedule()
+        scheduler.update_from_output(
+            output,
+            ModelRunnerOutput(
+                req_ids=[session.request_id],
+                req_id_to_index={session.request_id: 0},
+                sampled_token_ids=[[token]],
+            ),
+        )
+
+    step(4)
+    step(5)
+    assert session.status == RequestStatus.WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ
+    manager = scheduler.kv_cache_manager
+    old_block = manager.get_blocks(session.request_id).blocks[0][0]
+    old_key = old_block.block_hash
+    old_hash = session.block_hashes[0]
+    assert old_key is not None
+    old_probe = request("old", [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 100])
+    assert manager.get_computed_blocks(old_probe)[1] == block_size
+
+    scheduler.add_request(request("session", [42, 43, 44], resumable=True))
+    assert list(session.all_token_ids) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 42, 43, 44]
+    step(99)
+    assert session.block_hashes[0] == old_hash
+    assert old_block.block_hash == old_key
+    current = request("current", session.all_token_ids)
+    assert current.block_hashes[0] != old_hash
+    assert manager.get_computed_blocks(current)[1] == 0
+    if recovery == "resident":
+        return
+
+    if recovery == "reset":
+        assert scheduler.reset_prefix_cache(reset_running_requests=True)
+    else:
+        scheduler.running.remove(session)
+        scheduler._preempt_request(session, 0.0)
+    assert session.num_computed_tokens == 0
+    output = scheduler.schedule()
+    assert session.block_hashes == current.block_hashes
+    assert output.num_scheduled_tokens[session.request_id] == session.num_tokens
+    new_blocks, hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(current)
+    assert hit_tokens == block_size
+    old_blocks, old_hit_tokens, _ = manager.get_computed_blocks(old_probe)
+    if recovery == "reset":
+        assert old_hit_tokens == 0
+    else:
+        assert old_hit_tokens == block_size
+        assert old_blocks.blocks[0][0] is old_block
+        assert new_blocks.blocks[0][0] is not old_block
+        assert old_block.block_hash == old_key
+

+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+// SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+//
+// Per-architecture primitives of the Octave kernels. Every AMD target vLLM
+// builds compiles the portable tier; faster tiers are selected at runtime by
+// the host code (see docs/design/rocm_octave.md, "Architecture contract").
+//
+//   int8 dot4: v_dot4_i32_iu8 on gfx11/gfx12, v_dot4_i32_i8 on gfx9/gfx10.3
+//   decode, fast tier: octave_decode_wmma_rdna3.cu (WMMA, gfx11)
+//   prefill: octave_prefill_rdna3.cu (WMMA, gfx11)
+//   decode, portable: octave_attn.cu decode_kernel (dot4, every target)
+//
+// The portable kernels are written for 32-lane logical waves: shuffles never
+// cross 32 lanes, so they are correct on wave64 (CDNA) as well.
+
+#pragma once
+
+#include <cstdint>
+
+namespace octave {
+
+// sum_i a.i8[i] * b.i8[i] + c, signed bytes on both sides.
+__device__ __forceinline__ int dot4_i8(int a, int b, int c) {
+#if defined(__GFX11__) || defined(__GFX12__)
+  return __builtin_amdgcn_sudot4(true, a, true, b, c, false);
+#elif defined(__gfx942__)
+  return __builtin_amdgcn_sdot4(a, b, c, false);
+#else
+  #pragma unroll
+  for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i)
+    c += (int)(int8_t)(a >> (8 * i)) * (int)(int8_t)(b >> (8 * i));
+  return c;
+#endif
+}
+
+}  // namespace octave

+// fmt: V bits (3 or 4), plus 16 for compact K.
+void octave_cache_store(torch::Tensor key, torch::Tensor value,
+                        torch::Tensor cache, torch::Tensor slot_mapping,
+                        torch::Tensor k_signs, torch::Tensor v_signs,

+
+void octave_window_store(torch::Tensor key, torch::Tensor value,

@@ -0,0 +1,197 @@
+# Octave KV: a 3-bit KV cache for ROCm
+
+`ROCM_OCTAVE` is an attention backend for AMD GPUs that keeps the KV cache of
+full-attention layers at 3-4 bits per value, with native kernels (HIP today). It is
+selected with `--kv-cache-dtype octave_k3v3_compact`, `octave_k3v3` or
+`octave_k3v4` (the backend is picked from the cache dtype;
+`--attention-backend ROCM_OCTAVE` also works). The name comes from the 3-bit
+codes: each one indexes an eight-level codebook.
+
+## Why it exists
+
+Long-context serving on AMD GPUs is bounded by KV-cache memory long before it
+is bounded by compute. The existing options on ROCm were:
+
+- fp16/bf16 KV (`TRITON_ATTN`, `ROCM_ATTN`): 16 bits per value.
+- fp8 / int8 per-token-head: 8 bits per value.
+- `TURBOQUANT`: 3-4 bits per value, but its kernels are Triton (store and
+  decode) and its prefill goes through FlashAttention; it does not support the
+  fused multi-step MTP draft.
+
+Octave KV targets the same bit budget as TurboQuant with HIP kernels written for
+the AMD matrix instructions (WMMA on RDNA3, MFMA on CDNA as a contract slot),
+reading the packed cache directly in both decode and prefill, and with
+multi-token verification (MTP / speculative decoding) as a first-class case.
+
+## Supported models
+
+The format exploits *partial rotary embeddings*: models whose attention heads
+apply RoPE to a fraction of the head dims. Today the kernels are built for
+head size 256 with 64 rotary dims (`partial_rotary_factor = 0.25`), the
+attention shape of the Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8 family (dense
+and MoE, e.g. Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B). Like the MLA
+backends, which serve only models with multi-head latent attention, Octave KV is
+tied to an attention shape, not to a model.
+
+Models with full RoPE (Llama, Qwen3, Mistral, ...) or other head sizes are
+rejected at startup with an explicit error. Sliding window, ALiBi, attention
+sinks, soft-capping and encoder attention are not supported.
+
+The decode kernels cover GQA groups of 1, 2, 4, 6 or 8 query heads per KV
+head on each GPU. Under tensor parallelism the group is counted per GPU, so
+models with 32 query heads and 2 KV heads (Qwen3.5-122B-A10B) need TP ≥ 4.
+
+## Format
+
+One slot per (token, KV head). V is always rotated as one 256-dim block
+(random signs, then a Walsh-Hadamard transform) and gets 3 or 4 bits per dim.
+K has two layouts:
+
+- **Block K** (`octave_k3v3`, `octave_k3v4`): four 64-dim blocks, each rotated
+  on its own. The first block holds exactly the 64 rotary dims and gets 4 bits
+  per dim, the three NoPE blocks 3 bits; each block has its own scale.
+- **Compact K** (`octave_k3v3_compact`): rotated over all 256 dims like V,
+  3 bits per dim, one scale. The rotation spreads the rotary dims over the
+  whole head, so they need no extra bits; slots pad to 4 bytes instead of 8.
+
+| Bytes (block K) | Content |
+| --- | --- |
+| `[0, 32)` | K RoPE block, 4-bit codes |
+| `[32, 104)` | K NoPE blocks, 3-bit codes |
+| next `256·v/8` | V, `v`-bit codes |
+| next 10 | fp16 scales (K blocks 0-3, V) |
+
+| Bytes (compact K) | Content |
+| --- | --- |
+| `[0, 96)` | K, 3-bit codes |
+| `[96, 192)` | V, 3-bit codes |
+| `[192, 196)` | fp16 scales (K, V) |
+
+| Cache dtype | Slot bytes | Bits per value |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `octave_k3v3_compact` | 196 | 3.06 |
+| `octave_k3v3` | 216 | 3.38 |
+| `octave_k3v4` | 248 | 3.88 |
+
+For reference, `turboquant_3bit_nc` uses 198 bytes and `turboquant_k3v4_nc`
+230.
+
+After the rotation the coordinates are close to Gaussian, so each code
+indexes the Lloyd-Max codebook of N(0, 1) for its width, stored as int8
+(`LUT` in the reference): a code `c` of a block with scale `s` stands for
+`LUT[c] · s / 64`. The scale is chosen so that `x · x̂ = |x|²`. A
+least-squares fit minimizes the reconstruction error but shrinks every
+reconstructed vector (by about 3% at 3 bits), which flattens the softmax and
+scales down the attention output; at 380k tokens it cost 2-3× more NLL than
+this scale, at the same size. The quantizer is dynamic: no calibration, no per-model
+dictionaries. The kernels map four codes to their int8 values with one
+`v_perm_b32` (two for 4-bit codes), so the codebook costs nothing in
+bandwidth and the dot products stay integer. The byte layout's source of
+truth is the PyTorch reference in `vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_octave.py`.
+
+Why these layouts: measured on real Q/K/V of Qwen3.8-27B (32k tokens, every
+full-attention layer, attention-output error), both K layouts sit on the same
+bytes-versus-error curve, about 25-30% below TurboQuant at equal size; block
+K reaches the 4-bit rotary block, compact K the smallest slot. Rotating the
+rotary block alone at 3 bits does not work (one layer reaches 32% error);
+rotating it with the rest of the head does. Moving bits between K and V or
+weighting K channels by query energy did not help at a fixed size. The int8
+codebook loses nothing against the floating-point one.
+
+Attention runs in the rotated space: the query is rotated like K and the
+output is rotated back once per query. The rotations are orthogonal, so the
+scores are those of the unrotated vectors.
+
+## Kernels and data flow
+
+| Step | Kernel | File |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Cache write | `octave_cache_store`: one wave per slot, rotate + quantize + pack | `csrc/attention/octave_attn.cu` |
+| Decode / MTP verify (≤128 query tokens per request) | `octave_decode`: split-KV; WMMA tier on gfx11, portable dot4 tier elsewhere; consecutive query tokens of a request share each K/V read | `octave_decode_wmma_rdna3.cu`, `octave_attn.cu` |
+| Split reduce + inverse V rotation | `reduce_kernel` | `octave_attn.cu` |
+| Prefill | `octave_prefill`: phase 1 reads the cached prefix from the packed cache (int8 WMMA for QK with per-segment scales, fp16 WMMA for PV), phase 2 attends to the chunk's own unquantized K/V and merges | `octave_prefill_rdna3.cu` |
+| Q/K/V chunk rotation for prefill | `octave_rotate` | `octave_attn.cu` |
+| Codebooks (`v_perm_b32` tables) and byte layout | — | `octave_format.cuh` |
+
+The metadata builder builds, on the device and without host syncs, the
+per-query request and causal-length maps the kernels index by. They are what
+makes MTP verification batches (several query tokens per request, each with
+its own causal length) work without special cases, and they give cudagraph
+padding queries a K length of 0.
+
+## Architecture contract
+
+Kernels are native: HIP or FlyDSL, never Triton. There is no fallback: an
+architecture without a required kernel is rejected at startup with an error
+naming what is missing. The kernels in this tree are HIP; a FlyDSL kernel
+(for example a CDNA prefill) must keep the same signature and semantics, pass
+the same tests, and report a clear error when `flydsl` is not installed.
+
+Octave is enabled only on RDNA3 and CDNA3, validated on gfx1100 and gfx942
+(MI300). The backend rejects any other family at selection
+(`supports_compute_capability`, via `get_rdna_version()` and
+`get_cdna_version()`), and the kernel tests skip elsewhere. CMake builds the
+Octave sources and registers the ops only when the target list includes
+gfx1100 or gfx942; other targets in the same build compile the
+architecture-specific kernels as empty stubs, and the kernel dispatch reports
+any other RDNA3 chip as not validated.
+
+| Piece | gfx1100 (RDNA3) | gfx942 (MI300) |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| int8 dot4 (`octave_arch.cuh`) | `v_dot4_i32_iu8` | `v_dot4_i32_i8` |
+| Codebook lookup (`octave_format.cuh`) | `v_perm_b32` | `v_perm_b32` |
+| Cache store, reduce, rotate | portable | portable (decode reduce: gfx942 kernel) |
+| Decode | WMMA | MFMA (`v_mfma_i32_16x16x32_i8`) |
+| Prefill | WMMA | MFMA |
+
+The portable dot4 decode stays as the reference tier the tests compare the
+native tiers against.
+
+To add an architecture:
+
+1. Implement `octave_prefill` for it, in HIP or FlyDSL (same signature and semantics as
+   `octave_prefill_rdna3.cu`: phase-1 partials over the packed prefix, phase-2
+   chunk attention and merge, rotated space in and out).
+2. Add a decode tier, or validate the portable dot4 kernel there.
+3. Add the architecture to the CMake guard, to `_kernel_tier` and
+   `supports_compute_capability` in
+   `vllm/v1/attention/backends/rocm_octave_attn.py`, and to the test gate.
+4. Run `tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_octave.py`: every kernel is checked
+   against the PyTorch reference, and `test_decode_matches_reference` runs
+   both the fast and the portable decode tier.
+
+## Results
+
+All measurements on 4× RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100), Qwen3.8-27B W4A16, tensor
+parallel 4, MTP k=3, 8 GB of KV cache per GPU.
+
+### Capacity
+
+| KV cache | Tokens that fit |
+| --- | --- |
+| fp16 | TBD |
+| `turboquant_k3v4_nc` | 1,790,625 |
+| `octave_k4v4` | 1,402k |
+| `octave_k3v3` | 1,679k |
+
+### Speed
+
+TBD: `vllm bench serve` (random prompts, no prefix reuse) TTFT and TPOT at
+8k / 32k / 100k / 380k input, and per-layer kernel times from
+`benchmarks/attention_benchmarks`.
+
+### Quality
+
+TBD: GSM8K (`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 1319 questions, 5-shot,
+temperature 0.6) and next-token NLL over a 380k-token document.
+
+## Reproducing
+
+```bash
+vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --kv-cache-dtype octave_k3v4 ...
+pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_rocm_octave.py
+python benchmarks/attention_benchmarks/benchmark.py \
+    --backends ROCM_OCTAVE --kv-cache-dtype octave_k3v4 \
+    --model Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B --head-dim 256 --num-q-heads 6 --num-kv-heads 1 \
+    --batch-specs q1s100k q4s100k q2ks100k

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

+"""Octave HIP kernels against the PyTorch reference in
+vllm/v1/attention/ops/rocm_octave.py."""
+
+import math
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.v1.attention.utils import dense_kv_cache_views
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.rocm_octave_attn import RocmOctaveAttentionBackend
+from vllm.v1.attention.ops import rocm_octave as sq
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import FullAttentionSpec, get_kv_quant_mode
+
+
+def _arch() -> str | None:
+    if not current_platform.is_rocm():
+        return None
+    from vllm.platforms.rocm import get_cdna_version, get_rdna_version
+
+    if get_rdna_version() == 3:
+        return "rdna3"
+    return "cdna3" if get_cdna_version() == 3 else None
+
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    _arch() is None or not hasattr(torch.ops._C, "octave_decode"),
+    reason="Octave kernels need RDNA3 or CDNA3",
+)
+
+HEAD, ROPE, BLOCK = 256, 64, 16
+CACHE_DTYPES = ["octave_k3v4", "octave_k3v3", "octave_k3v3_compact"]
+
+
+def _format(cache_dtype: str) -> sq.OctaveFormat:
+    return sq.OctaveFormat.from_cache_dtype(cache_dtype, HEAD, ROPE)
+
+
+def _rel(a: torch.Tensor, b: torch.Tensor) -> float:
+    return ((a.float() - b.float()).norm() / b.float().norm()).item()
+
+
+def _token_slots(cache: torch.Tensor, slots: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """(blocks, H, block_size, slot) cache -> (T, H, slot) for flat slots."""
+    flat = cache.permute(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(-1, cache.shape[1], cache.shape[3])
+    return flat[slots]
+
+
+def _fill(cache, block_ids, k, v, k_signs, v_signs, fmt):
+    n = k.shape[0]
+    slots = (
+        block_ids.long().repeat_interleave(BLOCK)[:n] * BLOCK
+        + torch.arange(n, device=k.device) % BLOCK
+    )
+    torch.ops._C.octave_cache_store(
+        k, v, cache, slots, k_signs, v_signs, fmt.kernel_code
+    )
+    return slots
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cache_dtype", CACHE_DTYPES)
+def test_store_matches_reference(cache_dtype):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    dev, fmt = "cuda", _format(cache_dtype)
+    ksg = vsg = sq.sign_bits(HEAD).to(dev)
+    t, hkv = 1024, 2
+    k = torch.randn(t, hkv, HEAD, device=dev)
+    k[..., 100] *= 8  # an outlier channel is spread by the rotation
+    k = k.bfloat16()
+    v = torch.randn(t, hkv, HEAD, device=dev).bfloat16()
+    nblk = t // BLOCK + 4
+    cache = torch.zeros(nblk, hkv, BLOCK, fmt.slot_bytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
+    slots = _fill(cache, torch.randperm(nblk, device=dev), k, v, ksg, vsg, fmt)
+
+    k_got, v_got = sq.reference_dequantize(_token_slots(cache, slots), fmt)
+    ref = sq.reference_quantize(k.float(), v.float(), fmt)
+    k_ref, v_ref = sq.reference_dequantize(ref, fmt)
+    # Same codes up to rounding ties from a different summation order.
+    assert _rel(k_got, k_ref) < 1e-2 and _rel(v_got, v_ref) < 1e-2
+    # Lloyd-Max on Gaussian data: 3-bit codes (4-bit for block K's RoPE
+    # block) keep ~19% of the norm as error, 4-bit ~10%.
+    assert _rel(k_got, k) < 0.2
+    assert _rel(v_got, v) < (0.12 if fmt.v_bits == 4 else 0.22)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "cache_dtype,slot_bytes",
+    [("octave_k3v4", 248), ("octave_k3v3", 216), ("octave_k3v3_compact", 196)],
+)
+def test_slot_bytes_match_kernel_layout(cache_dtype, slot_bytes):
+    """The cache is sized from the Python format; the kernels index it with
+    octave::Format in csrc/attention/octave_format.cuh."""
+    assert _format(cache_dtype).slot_bytes == slot_bytes

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cache_dtype", CACHE_DTYPES)
+def test_store_skips_padding_slots(cache_dtype):
+    """Tokens with slot -1 (cudagraph padding) leave every byte unchanged."""
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    dev, fmt = "cuda", _format(cache_dtype)
+    ksg = vsg = sq.sign_bits(HEAD).to(dev)
+    t, hkv = 8, 2
+    k = torch.randn(t, hkv, HEAD, device=dev).bfloat16()
+    v = torch.randn(t, hkv, HEAD, device=dev).bfloat16()
+    cache = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (2, hkv, BLOCK, fmt.slot_bytes), dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev
+    )
+    before = cache.clone()
+    slots = torch.full((t,), -1, dtype=torch.long, device=dev)
+    slots[3] = 21
+    torch.ops._C.octave_cache_store(k, v, cache, slots, ksg, vsg, fmt.kernel_code)
+    written = torch.zeros_like(cache, dtype=torch.bool)
+    written[1, :, 5] = True
+    assert torch.equal(cache[~written], before[~written])
+    assert not torch.equal(cache[written], before[written])

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_wmma", [True, False])
+def test_decode_matches_reference(
+    cache_dtype, query_group, num_splits, dtype, use_wmma
+):
+    """Covers MTP verification: up to 4 consecutive query tokens per request,
+    each with its own causal length, plus a padded query with no request.
+    ``use_wmma=False`` forces the portable kernel every architecture runs."""
+    torch.manual_seed(1)
+    dev, fmt = "cuda", _format(cache_dtype)
+    ksg = vsg = sq.sign_bits(HEAD).to(dev)
+    hkv, group = 1, 6
+    lens = [1, 16, 37, 700, 3000]
+    cache = torch.zeros(512, hkv, BLOCK, fmt.slot_bytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
+    max_blocks = max(math.ceil(n / BLOCK) for n in lens)
+    block_table = torch.zeros(len(lens), max_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    free = torch.randperm(512, device=dev)
+    q_to_req, q_to_klen, used = [], [], 0
+    for i, n in enumerate(lens):
+        nb = math.ceil(n / BLOCK)
+        block_table[i, :nb] = free[used : used + nb].int()
+        used += nb
+        k = torch.randn(n, hkv, HEAD, device=dev).bfloat16()
+        v = torch.randn(n, hkv, HEAD, device=dev).bfloat16()
+        _fill(cache, block_table[i, :nb], k, v, ksg, vsg, fmt)
+        nq = min(query_group, n)
+        for j in range(nq):
+            q_to_req.append(i)
+            q_to_klen.append(n - nq + 1 + j)
+    q_to_req.append(len(lens) + 3)  # cudagraph padding: no request
+    q_to_klen.append(0)
+    q_to_req = torch.tensor(q_to_req, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    q_to_klen = torch.tensor(q_to_klen, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+
+    num_q = q_to_req.numel()
+    q = (torch.randn(num_q, hkv * group, HEAD, device=dev) * 2).to(dtype)
+    out = torch.zeros_like(q)
+    mid = torch.empty(
+        num_q, hkv * group, num_splits, HEAD + 2, dtype=torch.float32, device=dev
+    )
+    torch.ops._C.octave_decode(
+        out,
+        q,
+        cache,
+        block_table,
+        q_to_req,
+        q_to_klen,
+        mid,
+        ksg,
+        vsg,
+        1 / 16,
+        num_splits,
+        fmt.kernel_code,
+        query_group,
+        use_wmma,
+    )
+    ref = sq.reference_attention(
+        q.float(),
+        cache,
+        block_table,
+        q_to_req.clamp(max=len(lens) - 1),
+        q_to_klen,
+        fmt,
+        1 / 16,
+    )
+    # Only the kernel's query precision (fp16 or int8) differs.
+    assert _rel(out[:-1], ref[:-1]) < 2e-2
+    assert out[-1].abs().max().item() == 0
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("cache_dtype", CACHE_DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("query_lens", [[300], [129, 1, 517]])
+def test_prefill_matches_reference(cache_dtype, query_lens):
+    """Chunked prefill: each request's chunk attends causally to itself
+    (unquantized K/V) and to its cached prefix (packed cache), in the rotated
+    space the backend runs it in."""
+    torch.manual_seed(3)
+    dev, fmt = "cuda", _format(cache_dtype)
+    ksg = vsg = sq.sign_bits(HEAD).to(dev)
+    hkv, group = 1, 6
+    ctx_lens = [2500, 0, 4100][: len(query_lens)]
+    seq_lens = [c + n for c, n in zip(ctx_lens, query_lens)]
+    max_blocks = max(math.ceil(n / BLOCK) for n in seq_lens)
+    nblk = sum(math.ceil(n / BLOCK) for n in seq_lens) + 8
+    cache = torch.zeros(nblk, hkv, BLOCK, fmt.slot_bytes, dtype=torch.uint8, device=dev)
+    block_table = torch.zeros(len(seq_lens), max_blocks, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+    free, used = torch.randperm(nblk, device=dev), 0
+    ks, vs = [], []
+    for i, n in enumerate(seq_lens):
+        nb = math.ceil(n / BLOCK)
+        block_table[i, :nb] = free[used : used + nb].int()
+        used += nb
+        k = torch.randn(n, hkv, HEAD, device=dev).half()
+        v = torch.randn(n, hkv, HEAD, device=dev).half()
+        _fill(cache, block_table[i, :nb], k, v, ksg, vsg, fmt)
+        ks.append(k)
+        vs.append(v)
+
+    qsl = torch.tensor([0, *query_lens], device=dev).cumsum(0).int()
+    total = int(qsl[-1])
+    q = (torch.randn(total, hkv * group, HEAD, device=dev) * 2).half()
+    k_new = torch.cat([k[c:] for k, c in zip(ks, ctx_lens)])
+    v_new = torch.cat([v[c:] for v, c in zip(vs, ctx_lens)])
+    q_rot, k_rot, v_rot = q.clone(), k_new.clone(), v_new.clone()
+    torch.ops._C.octave_rotate(q_rot, ksg, not fmt.compact, False)
+    torch.ops._C.octave_rotate(k_rot, ksg, not fmt.compact, False)
+    torch.ops._C.octave_rotate(v_rot, vsg, False, False)
+    out = torch.empty_like(q_rot)
+    torch.ops._C.octave_prefill(
+        out,
+        q_rot,
+        k_rot,
+        v_rot,
+        cache,
+        block_table,
+        qsl,
+        torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev),
+        max(query_lens),
+        1 / 16,
+        fmt.kernel_code,
+    )
+    torch.ops._C.octave_rotate(out, vsg, False, True)
+
+    ref = torch.empty(total, hkv * group, HEAD, device=dev)
+    for i, (c, n) in enumerate(zip(ctx_lens, query_lens)):
+        k_all, v_all = ks[i][c:].float(), vs[i][c:].float()
+        if c > 0:
+            pos = torch.arange(c, device=dev)
+            slots = cache[block_table[i, pos // BLOCK].long(), :, pos % BLOCK]
+            k_pre, v_pre = sq.reference_dequantize(slots, fmt)
+            k_all, v_all = torch.cat([k_pre, k_all]), torch.cat([v_pre, v_all])
+        k_all = k_all.repeat_interleave(group, 1)
+        v_all = v_all.repeat_interleave(group, 1)
+        qi = q[int(qsl[i]) : int(qsl[i + 1])].float()
+        s = torch.einsum("qhd,thd->hqt", qi, k_all) / 16
+        mask = (
+            torch.arange(c + n, device=dev)[None]
+            > (c + torch.arange(n, device=dev))[:, None]
+        )
+        p = torch.softmax(s.masked_fill(mask, float("-inf")), -1)
+        ref[int(qsl[i]) : int(qsl[i + 1])] = torch.einsum("hqt,thd->qhd", p, v_all)
+    # Only the kernel's int8 query and fp16 P/V rounding differ.
+    assert _rel(out, ref) < 2e-2
+
+
+def _decode(cache, q, block_table, q_to_req, q_to_klen, signs, fmt, use_wmma):
+    out = torch.zeros_like(q)
+    mid = torch.empty(*q.shape[:2], 8, HEAD + 2, dtype=torch.float32, device=q.device)
+    torch.ops._C.octave_decode(
+        out,
+        q,
+        cache,
+        block_table,
+        q_to_req,
+        q_to_klen,
+        mid,
+        signs,
+        signs,
+        1 / 16,
+        8,
+        fmt.kernel_code,
+        1,
+        use_wmma,
+    )
+    return out
+
+
+def _prefill(cache, q, k, v, block_table, qsl, seq_lens, signs, fmt):
+    out = torch.empty_like(q)
+    torch.ops._C.octave_prefill(
+        out,
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        cache,
+        block_table,
+        qsl,
+        seq_lens,
+        int((qsl[1:] - qsl[:-1]).max()),
+        1 / 16,
+        fmt.kernel_code,
+    )
+    return out
+
